heading: INT. WKRT RADIO STATION - ON-AIR BOOTH - NIGHT

units.text: INT. WKRT RADIO STATION - ON-AIR BOOTH - NIGHT
A small studio with foam-padded walls and a console of dials.
A red ON AIR light glows over the glass.
Through the window, a dim control room.
JUNO FAIRWEATHER, 30s, the late-night host, in headphones and a cardigan, leans toward her microphone.
Across the console sits her producer, THEODORE "TEDDY" PAK, 30s, nervous, holding a clipboard.
On a stool by the door, ROSALIE MENDOZA-CLARK, 20s, a caller who has come in person, clutches a paper cup of coffee.
You're listening to the Midnight Hour. Our next caller is on line two. Hello, line two.
units.name: JUNO

units.text: Juno, hi. Long-time listener. I'm calling about someone in the room.
units.name: DAVID

units.text: Juno's eyes flick to Teddy.
Teddy shakes his head, mouthing "no."
Rosalie goes pale.
Is that right.
units.name: JUNO

units.text: I want to say something to Rosalie.
units.name: DAVID

units.text: Turn it off.
units.name: ROSALIE

units.text: Rosalie.
units.name: JUNO

units.text: Juno.
units.name: TEDDY

units.text: They speak at the same time.
I can't cut a caller on air.
units.name: JUNO

units.text: Cut the line, cut the line!
units.name: TEDDY

units.text: Rosalie shakes her head and takes a step toward the console.
I was a coward. I'm sorry. Will you marry me?
units.name: DAVID

units.text: Silence.
The red light burns.
Juno slowly slides her headphones off one ear.
Teddy drops the clipboard.
Rosalie stares at the speaker, then bursts into tears and laughter, and takes the microphone from Juno's hands.
Ask me in person.
units.name: ROSALIE
